The six classical calendar variation models

Source: R/classic.R
calvar_classic_all.Rd

Fits the six combinations of trend (deterministic or stochastic) and seasonality (dummy, Fourier or stochastic) of [calvar_classic()], named `m1` to `m6` as in its table.

Usage

calvar_classic_all(y, dates, K = frequency(y)/2 - 1, lambda = NULL, ...)

Arguments

y

Monthly or quarterly `ts`.

dates

`Date` vector of holiday occurrences.

K

Number of Fourier pairs for `season = "fourier"` (default 5 for monthly data).

lambda

Box-Cox parameter; `NULL` (default) keeps the original scale, so the holiday effect is additive.

...

Passed to [forecast::auto.arima()].

Value

An object of class `"calvar_classic_set"`: a list with the fitted models (`models`, named `m1` to `m6`) and their specification (`spec`).

Examples

# \donttest{
set <- calvar_classic_all(sapi, holiday_dates("idul_adha"))
set
#> Six classical calendar variation models
#>  model                                         structure
#>     m1           deterministic trend + dummy seasonality
#>     m2 deterministic trend + Fourier seasonality (K = 5)
#>     m3              stochastic trend + dummy seasonality
#>     m4    stochastic trend + Fourier seasonality (K = 5)
#>     m5      deterministic trend + stochastic seasonality
#>     m6         stochastic trend + stochastic seasonality
#>                    ARIMA effect    se AICc
#>             ARIMA(3,0,1)  29.78 1.716 1851
#>             ARIMA(3,0,1)  29.77 1.716 1849
#>             ARIMA(2,1,2)  29.78 1.725 1843
#>             ARIMA(2,1,2)  29.77 1.726 1841
#>  ARIMA(1,0,2)(2,0,0)[12]  17.61 1.905 1718
#>  ARIMA(1,1,1)(1,0,2)[12]  18.92 2.010 1709
#> Note: AICc is comparable only between models with the same order of differencing.
fc <- forecast(set, h = 12)
names(fc)
#> [1] "m1" "m2" "m3" "m4" "m5" "m6"
# }
